# Long-term experience needs storage, utility, and admission checks

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/agent-research/memory-and-skills.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-11 · 60 topic entries / 11 representative comparisons

MemGPT decides where information lives, MemPrice allocates fidelity within a limited window, and CMP studies how to identify utility. Voyager turns successful programs into skills, VaG manages admission risk, and SkillRise tests curation on later tasks. Fit, relevance, legitimacy, and future usefulness are four different questions. EMMA assigns structured memory to controller, agent, and skill, limiting each edit by failure scope and requiring actual use in the next attempt.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Allocation needs utility but does not create causal evidence

MemGPT moves information to archives, and MemPrice allocates representation levels within the window. Both need a keep decision. CMP studies identification instead: a memory retrieved disproportionately on difficult questions cannot be blamed for associated failures without randomized controls. When feeding CMP estimates into allocation, retain exposure design and uncertainty; net effects under fixed slots are not freely additive item values.

Sources: [MemGPT](../../../../agent-research/2310.08560-memgpt/README-en.md) · [MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents](../../../../agent-research/2610.24955-memprice/README-en.md) · [Causal Memory Policy: Making Memory Utility Identifiable by Intervening on Retrieval](../../../../agent-research/2610.02070-causal-memory-policy/README-en.md)

### Current success, durable admission, and future usefulness happen at different times

Voyager accumulates successful programs as skills. VaG considers effects on descendants, checking before write-back and assessing compatibility in use. SkillRise scores curation from downstream outcomes: current success mainly evaluates solving, not whether documentation helps later. These are different evidence contracts, not a ranking. Record execution, admission, and cross-task learning separately.

Sources: [Voyager](../../../../agent-research/2305.16291-voyager/README-en.md) · [When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents](../../../../agent-research/2608.05810-vag/README-en.md) · [SkillRise](../../../../agent-research/2607.26784-skillrise/README-en.md)

### October 29: New method and source changes

DiscernMem separates wrong memory scope from content defects. Pair single-memory and no-memory replays under the same task, seed, and configuration, then check repairs against both parent-memory and no-memory references. This constrains simple reflection append: poor team results cannot be blamed on one memory, and a new version cannot inherit old measured effects. Local work covers measurement and version contracts, not LLM repair or replay.

Sources: [MemGPT](../../../../agent-research/2310.08560-memgpt/README-en.md) · [Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems](../../../../agent-research/2610.36652-discernmem/README-en.md)

### Identify which entry to change, then show the change helps

DiscernMem uses isolated injection and paired no-memory replay to distinguish scope from defects and gates repairs against parent-memory and no-memory references. EMMA organizes editing by controller, agent specialization, and skill ownership; each reflection edits only one responsible entry, while execution slips affect only the temporary plan. One measures attribution and repair; the other limits the edit layer and how it must be exercised. Structural legality is not paired benefit, and an external semantic-safety Boolean is not an implemented LLM review.

Sources: [EMMA: Structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent Workflow Synthesis](../../../../agent-research/2610.35966-emma/README-en.md) · [Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems](../../../../agent-research/2610.36652-discernmem/README-en.md)

### Omitting a record from the current window does not prove the weights can replace it

MemPrice chooses which representations to read under a budget and utility estimate. After an external training update, ENGRAM compares a retrieval-free candidate with Base+ETG on the same probes to decide which training records may leave retrieval. The first saves window space without showing that the weights have learned the skill; the second tests local behavior without establishing end-to-end capability or total storage savings.

Sources: [MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents](../../../../agent-research/2610.24955-memprice/README-en.md) · [ENGRAM: From Agent Experience to Weights through Verified Consolidation](../../../../agent-research/2611.09472-engram-consolidation/README-en.md)

### Finding a relevant record and checking a lesson's source are different problems

MemFit preserves raw turns and uses summary indexing and hybrid retrieval to narrow candidates. WikiTrace links insights to interpretations and raw execution so a model can inspect why a lesson holds. Correct ranking cannot repair a false explanation; complete sources do not guarantee descent. Both local implementations are independent components: MemFit calls neither embeddings nor a cross-encoder, while WikiTrace calls neither a compiler LLM nor a test actor. Interface checks do not establish long-term question-answering gains.

Sources: [Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.14320-wikitrace/README-en.md) · [MemFit: Efficient Long-Term Agentic Memory](../../../../agent-research/2610.00872-memfit/README-en.md)

### Worth allocating memory and supported by enough evidence are separate axes

MemPrice jointly assigns fidelity levels under token limits using utility and long-run pressure. LiSA asks whether retrieved broad rules have enough evidence, while retaining narrow conflict cues. Cheap memory need not be reliable; reliable memory need not be budget-optimal. Both rely on external semantic inputs, so exact synthetic-input computations are not task-capability gains.

Sources: [LiSA: Lifelong Safety Adaptation via Conservative Policy Induction](../../../../agent-research/2605.14454-lisa/README-en.md) · [MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents](../../../../agent-research/2610.24955-memprice/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### If MemPrice selects a high-utility memory, why does CMP ask how utility was measured? {#cross-allocation-versus-identification}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Knapsack optimizes supplied utilities and sizes, not their reliability. Low success on tasks that often retrieve a memory can reflect selection bias. CMP uses balanced randomized exposure and controls to estimate net effect with a standard error. Slot substitution affects the result, so it cannot become an independent additive knapsack value unconditionally.

    **Illustrative example:** A troubleshooting memory is retrieved for the hardest incidents. Determine what happens without it before interpreting low success or budgeting window space.

    Sources: [MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents](../../../../agent-research/2610.24955-memprice/README-en.md) · [Causal Memory Policy: Making Memory Utility Identifiable by Intervening on Retrieval](../../../../agent-research/2610.02070-causal-memory-policy/README-en.md)

### Why can't a Voyager program that succeeded once enter VaG's long-term library unchecked alongside all other skills? {#cross-successful-skill-versus-admission}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** One execution supports that path under its environment, not harmlessness under other prerequisites or compatibility with existing skills. VaG checks structure, behavior, and semantics before writing, then chooses compatible sets by marginal value. Success, harmlessness, and combined benefits remain separate gates.

    **Illustrative example:** A skill works in an empty directory but implicitly deletes old files. The original success does not validate a shared directory.

    Sources: [Voyager](../../../../agent-research/2305.16291-voyager/README-en.md) · [When Self-Evolution Backfires: Pre-Commit Gating against Skill Contamination in LLM Agents](../../../../agent-research/2608.05810-vag/README-en.md)

### Why can't SkillRise use Voyager-style current success to reward curation directly? {#cross-current-outcome-versus-future-skill}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Current success measures actions just taken; a document's utility emerges on later related tasks. SkillRise separates solve and curate phases and applies discounted downstream returns to the latter's generated tokens. Successful program admission does not supply this cross-task credit. A polished but unhelpful summary should not be rewarded automatically.

    **Illustrative example:** A solver can succeed by luck but record only the answer. Downstream evaluation reveals the lack of reusable steps.

    Sources: [SkillRise](../../../../agent-research/2607.26784-skillrise/README-en.md) · [Voyager](../../../../agent-research/2305.16291-voyager/README-en.md)

### Why might a repaired memory that beats its parent still be rejected? {#cross-oct29-method-boundary}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** The parent can be harmful. A candidate must also match or beat no-memory, retain historical task performance, and not increase complete failures. One positive difference does not satisfy both non-regression references.

    **Illustrative example:** Parent memory scores 0.2, the repair 0.4, and no memory 0.8. Beating the parent does not establish usefulness.

    Sources: [MemGPT](../../../../agent-research/2310.08560-memgpt/README-en.md) · [Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems](../../../../agent-research/2610.36652-discernmem/README-en.md)

### Does EMMA's one-entry edit satisfy DiscernMem's causal attribution and repair checks? {#cross-emma-single-edit-versus-memory-effect}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. Single edits limit scope and clarify responsibility but still need actual exercise and rerun. DiscernMem separately uses paired isolated memory and no-memory results on matching tasks and seeds, then checks that the candidate is no worse than both parent and no-memory. Structure and effect have different acceptance conditions.

    **Illustrative example:** Writing a transient retrieval typo into a permanent skill violates EMMA scope. Correcting the skill text does not prove that memory helps more than omitting it.

    Sources: [EMMA: Structured Episodic Memory for Multi-Agent Workflow Synthesis](../../../../agent-research/2610.35966-emma/README-en.md) · [Remembering Is Not Enough: Refining Memories and Learning When to Use Them in Multi-Agent Systems](../../../../agent-research/2610.36652-discernmem/README-en.md)

### If MemPrice omits a record this round, can that signal directly approve ENGRAM memory release? {#cross-engram-approval-versus-window-budget}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. MemPrice allocates representations under a budget. ENGRAM also needs current training participation, reserved probes, and a retrieval-free candidate that clears both thresholds. An archived record is not deleted from physical storage.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: Two correct answers out of four require retention at a strict 50% floor, even when Base+ETG got only one correct.

    Sources: [MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents](../../../../agent-research/2610.24955-memprice/README-en.md) · [ENGRAM: From Agent Experience to Weights through Verified Consolidation](../../../../agent-research/2611.09472-engram-consolidation/README-en.md)

### If the most relevant lesson already ranks first, why does WikiTrace still need raw traces, and what does MemFit's retrieval test establish? {#cross-source-link-versus-memory-ranking}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Relevance determines what appears first, not whether a lesson is true or applicable. WikiTrace permits inspection of observations omitted by a summary. MemFit's local fusion hook checks externally supplied score composition, not model-computed semantic relevance or descent. Source fidelity, ranking and actual use need separate validation.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: a lesson says the task ended, but the raw trace contains a later submission. Ranking first does not fix the omission; a correct link does not establish the model notices it.

    Sources: [Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents](../../../../agent-research/2611.14320-wikitrace/README-en.md) · [MemFit: Efficient Long-Term Agentic Memory](../../../../agent-research/2610.00872-memfit/README-en.md)

### A short rule fits MemPrice's budget after one supporting observation. Why might LiSA still withhold it? {#cross-cross-memory-confidence-versus-capacity}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Capacity allocation and evidential reliability are distinct. A candidate's cost and utility can justify its representation without proving correctness. Beta(2,1)'s 5% quantile is about 0.22361, below 0.55. A narrow observed conflict cue instead follows the local channel's different rule.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: retain a ten-token rule in storage, but delay using it as general safety advice after only one success; separately surface public/private contextual boundary cues.

    Sources: [LiSA: Lifelong Safety Adaptation via Conservative Policy Induction](../../../../agent-research/2605.14454-lisa/README-en.md) · [MemPrice: Online Memory Allocation via Adaptive Pricing for Long-Horizon Agents](../../../../agent-research/2610.24955-memprice/README-en.md)
